name: Tunisia
summary: Tunisia follows an Islamic fixed-share system under the Personal Status Code of 1956 for Muslims. A foreigner's estate is governed by the law of their nationality under Law 98-97 (private international law code). Equal inheritance has been proposed but not enacted per the sources. Trusts and foundations were not sourced.
reserved_share: Muslims: fixed Islamic shares under the Personal Status Code (Decree of 13 Aug 1956); women inherit half a man's share.
foreign_law_note: Law 98-97 of 27 Nov 1998 (code de droit international privé) subjects inheritance to the deceased's nationality law; a renvoi exception if national law points to the place of the property. Heirs of a non-Muslim foreigner should obtain an embassy confirmation of that law.
trust_note: No trust (fiducie) or private-foundation law was found; answers provisional.
open_questions: Equal-inheritance reform status after 2018 not verified.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
